title: Read the current decision-verified provider run
description: Prerequisite for task-00e4827dd9374ec79625351d560c82c8; hard-depend on task-7e3ede6c76324017a1d53601940391f0, task-9d489aee991549a7ad0e414d69c381c8, and task-7f7fee6687944c7ab2116e05aab0bad8. Land the strict read-only project+attempt projection over canonical ProviderRunTelemetryCommitted events, binding each candidate to its command receipt/decision and the durable activation session/effect/epoch before any record gains authority.
definitionOfDone: A `readCurrentProviderRun(store,{projectId,attemptRef})`-style surface captures one event horizon and pages only `PROVIDER_RUN_EVENT_TYPE` through `readEventsByTypeAfter` with explicit page/candidate ceilings; it verifies every reserved provider event before filtering and never returns early on the first match or chooses a maximum epoch.

Each candidate is decoded/re-encoded by the production codec and must match its derived aggregate/event ids, sequence/version/schema, exported provider-run command kind, project/request trace, EFFECTS_COMMITTED 0->1 decision, singleton command receipt/effect digest, result bytes, and zero outbox; any readable disagreement is exact BINDING_MISMATCH.

The reader joins the unique task-7e3ede6c activation binding and requires exact attemptRef, effectIntentId, epoch, project and verified decision principal==ownerSessionRef; success is deeply frozen and returns the original durable ProviderRunRecord plus verified sessionId, recordDigest, stdoutReceiptDigest and captured horizon.

Zero matches is EVIDENCE_ABSENT, more than one is EVIDENCE_AMBIGUOUS, corrupt canonical bytes is RECORD_UNREADABLE, malformed page/envelope is EVIDENCE_MALFORMED, and store/decision/receipt absence or throw is EVIDENCE_UNREADABLE with exact layer/upstream storeCode; all answers grant zero authority.

Real SqliteEventStore tests cover an accepted record, more than one page of foreign records before the match, a duplicate after a page boundary, absent, corrupt, foreign project/session, cursor drift, horizon racing, and a positive mutation table for aggregate/event/trace/decision/result/receipt bindings; raw event/decision counts prove the reader writes nothing.

Mutation drills skipping receipt validation or selecting the first duplicate redden named assertions; daemon typecheck/test count lines are nonzero and completion names task-00e4827dd9374ec79625351d560c82c8 and task-ded026d6587442eabc28ff2609d231aa as consumers.

implementationPlan.description:
THE BOUNDED SCAN — DoD item 1, and every clause of it is a trap that has been hit before on this board.
- Capture ONE horizon via `readEventHorizon()` BEFORE paging, and re-read it after the scan; a horizon that moved means the scan judged a ledger that no longer exists -> refuse (no partial answer). This mirrors what `readFoundationActivationByAttempt` does at activation-attempt-reader.ts:243-245.
- Page ONLY `PROVIDER_RUN_EVENT_TYPE` through `readEventsByTypeAfter` with the explicit page limit. Never scan all event types (task rail 2), and never use raw DatabaseSync.
- CURSOR DISCIPLINE: advance strictly by the page's own `nextCursor`; if it does not advance past the previous position, refuse rather than loop. Stop on `hasMore === false`. A malformed page or envelope -> `PROVIDER_RUN_EVIDENCE_MALFORMED`.
- VERIFY EVERY RESERVED PROVIDER EVENT BEFORE FILTERING. The DoD says this explicitly: a row of this reserved event type that fails verification is a fact about the ledger, not noise to skip past. Filtering first and verifying later would let a corrupt row be silently dropped and a later duplicate read as the unique match.
- NEVER RETURN EARLY ON FIRST MATCH, and never choose a maximum epoch. Collect ALL candidates to the ceiling, then decide: zero -> `PROVIDER_RUN_EVIDENCE_ABSENT`; more than one -> `PROVIDER_RUN_EVIDENCE_AMBIGUOUS`. Selecting the first or the highest epoch would turn an ambiguity — which demands a human — into a confident wrong answer.
implementationPlan.note:
BOUNDED SCAN LANDED. `scanForAttempt` in provider-run-reader.ts.

WHAT IT DOES, clause by clause:
- ONE horizon captured before paging and re-read in `settle` before ANY answer leaves the module, refusing EVIDENCE_UNREADABLE if it moved. Every exit path routes through `settle` — success and refusal alike — so there is no branch that returns an answer judged against a horizon it never re-checked.
- Pages ONLY `PROVIDER_RUN_EVENT_TYPE` through `readEventsByTypeAfter` at the module's own PAGE_SIZE. No all-type scan, no raw DatabaseSync.
- CURSOR DISCIPLINE: strictly increasing `globalPosition` within a page, `page.nextCursor` must equal the last position reached, `hasMore === false` stops, and a page that yielded nothing while claiming more refuses instead of looping.
- `wellShaped` re-checks the page envelope (object, boolean hasMore, array items, items <= PAGE_SIZE, nextCursor bigint|null) before it is trusted.
- VERIFIES EVERY RESERVED ROW BEFORE COMPARING THE ATTEMPT. A refusal from verification returns immediately rather than being skipped, so a corrupt neighbour cannot be dropped silently and leave a later duplicate reading as unique.
- NO EARLY RETURN AND NO MAXIMUM EPOCH: the walk continues after a hit; a second match is `PROVIDER_RUN_EVIDENCE_AMBIGUOUS`, zero is `PROVIDER_RUN_EVIDENCE_ABSENT`.
- Ceilings: MAX_PAGES 64 and MAX_CANDIDATES 6400, both `>=`/`>` guarded so they can actually fire, both refusing EVIDENCE_UNREADABLE rather than truncating.

implementationPlan.description:
PER-CANDIDATE VERIFICATION — DoD item 2. Decode each candidate through the PRODUCTION codec (`decodeProviderRunRecord`), then re-derive and compare, refusing `PROVIDER_RUN_BINDING_MISMATCH` (storeCode null) on any readable disagreement and `PROVIDER_RUN_RECORD_UNREADABLE` when the canonical bytes themselves cannot be trusted:
- aggregate id equals `deriveProviderRunAggregateId(record.providerRunRef)` and event id equals `deriveProviderRunEventId(...)`. Both are length-framed domain-separated digests; re-derive from the DECODED ref, never from the event's own fields, or the check agrees with itself.
- record version / schema and the event's aggregate sequence and version are what the ledger writes.
- the decision for this candidate's command has `commandKind === PROVIDER_RUN_COMMAND_KIND` — the exported constant, never a local string.
- project and request/correlation trace agree.
- the decision is an `EffectsCommittedDecision`: `effectDisposition === "EFFECTS_COMMITTED"` with `previousVersion` 0 and `currentVersion` 1. A `NoBusinessEffectDecision` carries `resultCode: "EXPECTED_VERSION_CONFLICT"` and is NOT a committed run.
- `businessEventIds` is the singleton naming this event, `outboxMessageIds` is EMPTY, and `getCommandReceipt(commandId)` returns a receipt whose effect digest and result bytes match the decision's. Zero outbox is asserted, not assumed.
A decision or receipt that is absent, or a store call that throws, is `PROVIDER_RUN_EVIDENCE_UNREADABLE` with the store's own code preserved in `storeCode` — never restamped into a reader code (task rail 3).

- AGGREGATE ID: `event.aggregateId !== deriveProviderRunAggregateId(record.providerRunRef)`. Re-derived from the DECODED ref, never from the event's own fields — that is the difference between a check that can fail and one that agrees with itself, and drill 5 is aimed at exactly this.
- EVENT ID: `event.eventId !== deriveProviderRunEventId(record.providerRunRef)`, same discipline, different domain.
- SEQUENCE / VERSION / SCHEMA: `event.aggregateSequence === 1`, `record.recordVersion === PROVIDER_RUN_RECORD_VERSION`, and on the decision `expectedVersion 0`, `observedVersion 0`.
- COMMAND KIND: compared against the exported `PROVIDER_RUN_COMMAND_KIND` on BOTH the trace and the decision. No local string literal anywhere in the module.
- PROJECT / REQUEST TRACE: `trace.projectId === projectId`, `decision.key.projectId === trace.projectId`, `decision.key.commandId === trace.commandId`, `decision.key.principalId === trace.principalId`, `decision.requestSha256 === trace.requestSha256`.

- SINGLETON / ZERO OUTBOX / RESULT BYTES: `businessEventIds.length === 1 && businessEventIds[0] === event.eventId`, `outboxMessageIds.length === 0`, `sameBytes(decision.resultBytes, event.payload)`.
- RECEIPT: `getCommandReceipt(event.commandId)` — the STORE-internal command id, NOT the trace's request command id; those are different ids and swapping them reads null, so each is named at its own call. - `sameBytes` keeps its `instanceof Uint8Array` pair: two non-binary payloads both report an `undefined` byteLength, so without it a contract-breaking store reaches `.every` and CRASHES where this module must refuse. A crash is not a refusal.

TWO DOMAINS KEPT APART, mirroring the activation reader's own note: the DECISION's `requestSha256` is the SCOPED-COMMAND digest and is compared to the TRACE's; the RECEIPT's is the EFFECT digest and is compared to the EVENT's. Comparing either across domains would be a check that can never pass.

THE ACTIVATION JOIN — DoD item 3. Call `readFoundationActivationByAttempt(store, projectId, attemptRef)` and require `status === "BOUND"`. Its refusal is returned with ITS OWN code and layer preserved verbatim: it has its own `FOUNDATION_ACTIVATION_BINDING_LAYER` and a mandatory `storeCode`, and flattening either would make an absent activation indistinguishable from an unreadable store.
Then require EXACT agreement between the decoded record and the binding: `attemptRef`, `effectIntentId`, `epoch`, `projectId`, and — per step 2's resolution — `decision.key.principalId === binding.ownerSessionRef`. Any disagreement is `PROVIDER_RUN_BINDING_MISMATCH`.
NEVER INFER (task rail 3): not the session from attempt order, not currentness or terminality from `FoundationAttemptRecorded`, not the exit from anything. The binding is the only authority for session and epoch, and it is obtained by the landed reader rather than re-derived here — a second lookup would be a second answer that can disagree with the first.
SUCCESS SHAPE, deeply frozen: the ORIGINAL durable `ProviderRunRecord` (not a rebuilt lookalike), the verified `sessionId` (= ownerSessionRef), `recordDigest`, `stdoutReceiptDigest`, and the captured horizon. Every refusal arm carries zero authority and no partial record.

implementationPlan.description:
THE REFUSAL AND SCAN MATRIX — DoD items 4 and 5. Every case asserts the exact code, the exact LAYER, and the exact `storeCode` (a `DurableStoreErrorCode` or null), because this family deliberately keeps three EVIDENCE_* answers apart and a test asserting only `ok === false` would stay green if they merged.
- ACCEPTED, then: MORE THAN ONE PAGE of foreign provider-run rows before the match — seed enough committed runs for OTHER attempts to force at least two pages, proving the scan pages rather than reading one batch.
- A DUPLICATE AFTER A PAGE BOUNDARY -> `PROVIDER_RUN_EVIDENCE_AMBIGUOUS`. This is the case that catches an early return: a reader that stops at the first match passes every other test in this file.
- ABSENT -> `PROVIDER_RUN_EVIDENCE_ABSENT`; corrupt canonical bytes -> `PROVIDER_RUN_RECORD_UNREADABLE`; malformed page/envelope -> `PROVIDER_RUN_EVIDENCE_MALFORMED`; a store whose reader throws -> `PROVIDER_RUN_EVIDENCE_UNREADABLE` with the store's code verbatim.
- FOREIGN PROJECT and FOREIGN SESSION, as two separate cases with distinct expected outcomes.
- CURSOR DRIFT (a page whose `nextCursor` does not advance) and HORIZON RACING (the horizon moves between the two reads) -> refuse, with no partial answer.
- A GENERATED MUTATION TABLE over the aggregate / event id / trace / decision / result bytes / receipt bindings: assert `cases.length > 0` BEFORE asserting outcomes — a generated table that silently produces zero cases passes while testing nothing — and assert each mutation refuses with `PROVIDER_RUN_BINDING_MISMATCH` rather than throwing. A crash is not a refusal.
After EVERY arm, assert raw event and decision counts are unchanged.
implementationPlan.note:
REFUSAL AND SCAN MATRIX COMPLETE. `Tests 57 passed (57)` (up from 53); tsc clean on my paths.

EVERY ARM PINS CODE + LAYER + storeCode by `toStrictEqual` over the whole refusal object, so a merged EVIDENCE_* pair, a moved layer or a swallowed storeCode all redden. Every arm also asserts `snapshot(store)` — raw event count, raw command-decision count and horizon — unchanged, each taken through `positiveSnapshot` which asserts all three POSITIVE first so an all-zero comparison cannot pass.

STEP-8 CHECKLIST, item by item, all present:
- ACCEPTED control; MORE THAN ONE PAGE of foreign rows before the match (PAGE_SIZE+5 seeded, with an independent assertion that page 1 is full and hasMore is true).
- DUPLICATE AFTER A PAGE BOUNDARY -> EVIDENCE_AMBIGUOUS, with an independent assertion that the duplicate's aggregate is NOT on page 1. This is the arm that catches an early return.
- ABSENT; RECORD_UNREADABLE (one flipped byte inside the sealed body); EVIDENCE_MALFORMED over seven page/envelope shapes; a throwing pager -> EVIDENCE_UNREADABLE with STORE_UNAVAILABLE verbatim.
- FOREIGN PROJECT and FOREIGN SESSION as two separate arms whose outcomes are distinct in WHICH LAYER ANSWERED, not merely in code: the foreign-project arm runs against a pager that always throws, so BINDING_MISMATCH there proves the project gate answered before anything was scanned, while the foreign-session arm completes a real scan and can only be refused by the principal join.
- CURSOR DRIFT and HORIZON RACING, both refusing with no partial answer; the horizon arm also asserts the second read actually happened (`reads > 1`).
- GENERATED MUTATION TABLE with `length > 0`, an exact length and name-uniqueness asserted in their OWN test before any outcome.

FIVE GAPS FOUND BY AUDITING THE MATRIX AGAINST THE CHECKLIST, all closed:
1. "A CRASH IS NOT A REFUSAL" was implied, not asserted — a throw from production would have failed the test with a stack trace rather than an assertion. Added `readWithoutThrowing`, which records any escaping throw and asserts it is null, and routed the whole mutation table plus the new arms through it.
2. A CONTRACT-BREAKING (non-binary) `resultBytes` was untested, so the `instanceof Uint8Array` pair in production's `sameBytes` — the one that stops `.every` being called on a value that has no such method — was unguarded. Added as mutation 21; it refuses BINDING_MISMATCH and provably does not throw. Table count updated 20 -> 21.
3. A RESERVED ROW WITH NO `decisionTrace` was untested. Added -> EVIDENCE_MALFORMED (evidence that never arrived is not evidence that disagrees). The key is DELETED rather than set to undefined: under `exactOptionalPropertyTypes` those are different shapes and only the deletion is what a store that never wrote a trace hands back. Setting it to undefined was in fact rejected by tsc — TS2375 — which is how the distinction surfaced.
4. A NON-STORE THROW was untested, so "a foreign throw invents none" was unpinned. Added a `TypeError` from the pager -> EVIDENCE_UNREADABLE with storeCode NULL, next to the DurableStoreError arm that carries STORE_UNAVAILABLE. Together they pin both halves of `refuseThrown`.
5. PROVIDER_RUN_READER_MAX_PAGES was an UNREACHABLE branch in the existing arms: with full 100-row pages the candidate ceiling always fires first (6400 = 64 x 100), so the page bound was never exercised. Added an arm serving ONE real foreign row per page with a strictly advancing cursor, where the candidate ceiling cannot fire, and it reaches the page bound -> EVIDENCE_UNREADABLE. Without it a pager serving short pages forever was an unbounded walk that no test would have caught.

TOTAL: 57 cases. 22 in the mutation group (21 generated + the generation guard), 2 production-seeded join cases (foreign effect intent, foreign epoch), 21 in the unreadable-bytes/pages/stores group, plus the accepted, count, query/project and activation-passthrough groups.
